I have 10.1 mu and four crops to manage. Let me think through this carefully — I only started farming two years ago, so I watch my neighbors closely and mostly do what they do.

**Splitting my land:**
Most of my land goes to the wheat-maize double crop like everyone around here — it's the backbone in Quzhou. I'll put 6.1 mu on wheat-maize rotation. That gives us food for the family and steady grain income. Then 2 mu for chili and 2 mu for eggplant — vegetables bring more money but they cost more and need more work. I won't plant more vegetables than that because my wife and I can only handle so much picking, and my son is still in school.

**Wheat (winter, 6.1 mu):** Last year I used about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (25 kg each) plus a bag of urea at jointing. That's about 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. Neighbors get 450–500 kg/mu and so did I. I'll do the same — no reason to change when it worked. Two irrigations from the well (winter and jointing), one spray for aphids and powdery mildew. Rotary tillage because that's what the tractor service offers.

**Maize (summer, 6.1 mu):** After wheat, I plant hybrid maize directly — no tillage, just seed into the stubble like the agricultural station told us. One bag compound at sowing, one bag urea at big trumpet stage — roughly 20 kg N, 6 kg P, 5 kg K. One irrigation if July is dry. One pesticide for armyworm. I aim for 550 kg/mu.

**Chili (spring-autumn, 2 mu):** This is where I need to be careful — chili needs a lot of feeding or the fruits stay small. I'll use manure base plus compound fertilizer, about 28 kg N, 15 kg P, 20 kg K per mu across the season. Drip from the well, 8 irrigations because the ground dries fast in summer. Pest pressure is heavy — aphids, thrips, anthracnose — probably 6 sprays. Improved variety seedlings from the county market. If I get 2200 kg/mu I'm happy.

**Eggplant (spring-autumn, 2 mu):** Similar to chili but eggplant eats even more potassium. 30 kg N, 15 kg P, 25 kg K per mu. 10 irrigations — eggplant wilts fast without water. 7 sprays for whitefly, mites, and fruit rot. Plough before transplanting to loosen the soil deep for the roots. Hybrid seedlings. Aim for 3500 kg/mu.

I'd rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose fruit — a bad harvest would really hurt us, wasting some fertilizer is just money.
